# Abstract

The Open Cooperative Perception System (O-CPS) is an open, manufacturer-agnostic cooperative perception and control layer for road vehicles and roadside infrastructure. It reuses existing V2X radio, network, and security standards (C-V2X PC5 / NR-V2X sidelink, ITS-G5, SAE J2735, SAE J3161, ETSI TS 103 324, IEEE 1609.2, ETSI TS 103 097) and adds three primitives that the current standards ecosystem leaves underspecified: a normalized perception profile that allows vehicles with radically different sensor suites to exchange a common world model; a fusion and trust framework that produces calibrated confidence in multi-source object tracks; and a Cooperative Adaptive Cruise Control (C-ACC) Group Protocol that allows driver-authorized platoons to form, persist, hand off leadership, and dissolve without cloud dependence.

This document is the v0.2 specification draft. It is the successor to the v0.1 draft circulated in August 2025. Relative to v0.1 it adds: a complete wire-format schema for the full message set; a formal trust model with continuous attestation and misbehavior revocation; a safety architecture aligned to ISO 26262 with explicit ASIL allocation per message class; a conformance-class framework; and the Slipstream Mode overlay introduced as an optional application-layer extension.

O-CPS is a standards and influence play, not a product. It is published in the open, with a permissive license posture, to give automakers, suppliers, municipalities, and fleet operators a shared target to converge on rather than a vendor-specific lock-in.
